Pool Bucket Test: Is Your Pool Leaking or Evaporating?

By SRQ Leak Pros Editorial · Published November 5, 2026 · Updated November 6, 2026 · 6 min read

Short answer: A pool bucket test compares water loss in your pool with water loss in a bucket sitting on the pool step. Both lose water to evaporation. If the pool drops more than the bucket over 2 to 3 days, you likely have a leak. Repeat with the pump on and then off to see whether the leak is in the plumbing or the shell.

Every pool loses some water to sun and wind. The question is whether yours is losing more than that. The pool bucket test answers it with a bucket, a marker and a few days of patience. If the test points to a leak, SRQ Leak Pros can connect you with a local provider for pool leak detection in Sarasota to find it.

What is a pool bucket test?

It's a side-by-side check. A bucket of pool water sits on a step in the pool, so it gets the same sun, heat and wind. The bucket can only lose water to evaporation. The pool can lose water to evaporation and to a leak. Compare the two drops and you know which one you have.

What you need

  • A bucket, such as a 5-gallon pail
  • A waterproof marker, grease pencil or wax pen
  • Something to weigh the bucket, such as a brick, if needed
  • A calm, rain-free stretch of 2 to 3 days

How to do a pool bucket test

These steps follow the City of Scottsdale's water conservation guide.

  1. Fill the pool to its normal level. Then stop adding water.
  2. Turn off the autofill. If your pool has one, close the valve on its supply line.
  3. Don't backwash or splash. Any lost water skews the result.
  4. Set the bucket on a pool step. Don't let it float or sink below the waterline.
  5. Fill the bucket to match the pool level. Water inside should line up with water outside.
  6. Mark both levels. Mark the water line inside the bucket and the pool level on the outside of the bucket or the tile.
  7. Wait 2 to 3 days. Keep the pump on its normal schedule.
  8. Compare the drops. Measure how far each level fell.

If it rains or turns very windy, start over. Scottsdale notes that rain or wind may mean you need to redo the test.

How to read your bucket test results

ResultWhat it meansNext step
Pool and bucket dropped the sameEvaporation, no leakReduce evaporation
Pool dropped more than the bucketLikely leakRun the pump-on, pump-off test
Bucket dropped more than the poolTest error, or water was addedCheck the autofill and retest
Unclear or tiny differenceInconclusiveRetest on a calm day

Pump on vs. pump off: where is the leak?

If the first test shows a leak, run it twice more. Once with the pump running on its normal schedule. Once with the pump off the whole time.

  • More loss with the pump on. The leak is likely in the pressure side of the plumbing, such as return lines or equipment.
  • More loss with the pump off. The leak is more likely in the pool structure, such as the shell, light niche or skimmer.
  • Same loss either way. The leak may be in the shell below the skimmer or in a fitting that leaks under any condition.

Scottsdale's guide uses this same logic. If more water is lost with the pump running, the plumbing is the likely cause.

Other signs your pool is leaking

Scottsdale's guide lists these signs:

  • Visible leaks on the pool equipment
  • Wet spots between the equipment and the pool
  • White, crusty mineral deposits on pipes, which can mean a slow leak
  • An autofill that seems to run nonstop
  • A pool level that drops faster than the bucket

Other clues include cracks in the deck or tile, loose tiles, air bubbles at the return jets and a higher water bill.

How do pros find a pool leak?

A pool leak pro starts with your bucket test results. Common methods include:

  • Dye testing. Dye near a crack or fitting shows whether water is being pulled out.
  • Pressure testing. Each pool line is plugged and pressurized to see if it holds.
  • Listening gear. Underwater and ground microphones hear water escaping.
  • Visual dive inspection. A close look at the shell, lights, skimmers and drains.

Angi's data, updated February 2024, puts pool leak detection at about $100 to $1,000, with an average of about $300. Repairs are priced separately.

How to reduce evaporation if there's no leak

  • Use a pool cover when the pool isn't in use.
  • Add a windbreak, such as a hedge or screen.
  • Lower the water temperature if you heat the pool.
  • Turn off waterfalls and fountains when you can.
  • Keep the water at the proper level for the skimmer.

Pool bucket tests in Sarasota

Sarasota's sun, heat and wind can make evaporation high, so a falling pool doesn't always mean a leak. That's why the side-by-side test matters. Summer afternoon storms can add water and ruin a test, so pick a dry stretch. Many local pools sit under screen enclosures, which can cut wind but not heat. Pools near the coast may also see stronger breezes.

A pool leak also wastes water that you pay for. The EPA says the average home's leaks waste more than 9,300 gallons a year, before counting a pool.

Florida rules to know

Pool equipment and plumbing work may need a permit, depending on the repair and your city or county. Ask the provider whether a permit is needed. Check the license of anyone repairing pool plumbing or structure on the DBPR site.

Local note: screened pools are common in Lakewood Ranch and Venice. Coastal pools on Siesta Key and Longboat Key face more wind, so run the test on a calm day.

Related reading: if the bucket test rules out the pool, check for an irrigation leak or a water meter leak. A high bill can come from many places, so see why your water bill is so high.

When should you call a pool leak professional?

Call a pro when:

  • The pool drops faster than the bucket
  • The pump-on test shows more loss than the pump-off test
  • You see wet spots near equipment or cracks in the deck
  • Your autofill runs nonstop or your bill jumped

Frequently asked questions

How long should a pool bucket test run?

Many guides use 2 to 3 days. Longer tests make small leaks easier to see, as long as weather stays calm and dry.

How much water does a pool lose to evaporation?

It varies with sun, heat, wind and humidity. That's why the bucket test compares the pool with a bucket under the same conditions.

Can a pool leak through the skimmer?

Yes. The skimmer can separate from the pool wall or crack. A dye test near the skimmer helps confirm it.

Should the pump be on during a bucket test?

Run the first test with the pump on its normal schedule. If you find a leak, test again with it off to compare.

Does a pool cover affect the bucket test?

A cover cuts evaporation, but it can also hide the bucket comparison. Run the test uncovered for a clean result.
